title: MV Earliest of early stages of my project

posts.author: Pongolho
posts.body:
So, this is my first post on the forum whatsoever. I've been messing around with Rpg Maker since forever, then I stopped and started messing around with digital art and pixel art. So lately I've been wanting to cook up a little game on my own on my free time. I admit I'm not very good at programming, but I have a story to tell and moderate art skills. So, here it is what I proudly have already:
A vision and many hopes and optism
A main character sprite and portrait
Main character's house/hub map art
I'll definitely use parallax maps, pixel movement and custom collisions so that I can make this style playable.
I also want to work with ABS, since is highly customizable and I'll be able to attain something like Legend of Mana or Odin Sphere, which are my main inspirations and references.
I really like MV's bigger graphics as it fits really nice into my map creating technique and aestethic. I'm aware that making a whole game like that by myself will be challenging to say the least, but I have SO much fun playing with tiles in photoshop, changing their perspective to fit my view.
I'm at the stage where I'm building the earliest most earlier foundations yet, like gathering scripts and tools, learning animation and parallax mapping, getting to know the engine and etc. But I learn fast!
So here's what I have to show:
Main character protoype walking exercise(a little bumpy):
Main character portrait:
And what I've been having the most fun doing: MAPPING! Or you can say... drawing?
All tilesets used are free and I have all the authors' names written so I can credit them properly.
Story and plot is still in its roots. The story happens on a post-post-apocaliptic world, meaning the world already ended and humanity is rebuilding in this new torn and warped world.
I want to bring several cultures and arquitectures into my design, since i'ts something I really like, also with elements of various folklores and myths.
So, that's it. Tell me what you think! Be aware that this is my first try at any of this, so criticize away!

posts.author: TheSyntheticForest
posts.body:
Great design on the main character! Have you heard of dragonbones animation software before? I use in on RMMZ and it makes animating a lot of fun! It's a little technical at first but powerful once you figure out how to get it to work! It may make it easier for you once you try to incorporate different characters as well, def worth it to check it out!
Here is a link for the plugin for RMMV
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/index.php?threads/rmmv-dragonbones-2d-animation-integration.81027/

posts.author: Roocifer
posts.body: I love your art! MY only critique is the pathway behind the building being too unusual, if you want an incline, the use of more shadows and perspective is needed. I believe Photoshop has a perspective ruler, it's been a long time since I used an Adobe product. Other than that, it's super crisp, interesting, and I love looking at all the details you have. Keep up the great work!!
